memory_candidates.content: When relocating a runtime-file path that multiple scripts derive by string concatenation and a shared class-tracking lib enumerates by index-aligned parallel arrays (e.g. runtime-file-patterns.sh's RUNTIME_FILE_IDS/PATTERNS/PROBES/B_REGEX/IS_DIR/DIR_BASENAME), add a single shared path-resolver function to the lib (e.g. runtime_mt_state_path(specs_dir, session_id)) rather than updating N independent string-literal derivations across N writer/reader scripts. This reduces future rename cost to one call site and makes drift between writers structurally impossible. Also: adding a new lib source line to a widely-tested script (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh) breaks every hand-maintained test-fixture sandbox that copies that script's dependencies by an explicit list/array rather than a wildcard -- grep the whole scripts/tests/ tree for sandboxes building the SAME script before considering the source-line addition complete, since a full run-all.sh pass is the only reliable way to surface all of them (some sandboxes carry zero literal references to the relocated path, so a ref-count grep alone misses them).

When a full run-all.sh pass surfaces test failures unrelated to the current task's edits, use `git merge-base --is-ancestor <file's-last-touch-commit> <commit-that-introduced-the-now-unmet-dependency>` to prove a failure predates the current task, rather than assuming or hand-waving 'probably pre-existing'. Pair with `git stash` + re-run for failures with no clear introducing commit (confirms the failure reproduces identically with zero current-task changes present). This produces citable evidence for a plan's #### Reasoned Exclusions table (the [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] phase-heading marker's required record) instead of an unsubstantiated claim.
